default.title: BUY OR RENT?
default.speaker: Property agent
default.intro: You earn ₹50,000 a month. Rent now: ₹12,000.
default.text: '₹40 lakh flat! Home-loan EMI just ₹35,000 a month for 20 years. Book today, prices go up tomorrow!'

pocket_money.title: BUY OR RENT?
pocket_money.speaker: Property agent
pocket_money.intro: You earn ₹50,000. Your parents want 'our own house' before they retire.
pocket_money.text: '₹40 lakh flat, EMI ₹35,000 a month for 20 years. Your parents will be so proud. Book today!'

scholarship.title: BUY OR RENT?
scholarship.speaker: Property agent
scholarship.intro: You earn ₹50,000. Relatives keep asking when you'll 'settle down' in your own flat.
scholarship.text: '₹40 lakh, EMI ₹35,000 a month for 20 years. Only two flats left on this floor!'

earner.title: BUY OR RENT?
earner.speaker: Property agent
earner.intro: You earn ₹50,000 and still send money home every month.
earner.text: '₹40 lakh flat, EMI just ₹35,000 a month for 20 years. Prices only go up!'

choices.lesson: An EMI that eats 70% of income leaves nothing for food, shocks or savings. Over 20 years you'd repay about ₹84 lakh.

effects.label: Saving for a bigger down payment

choices.lesson: Keep EMIs under about a third of income. A bigger down payment means a smaller loan and far less interest.
An EMI at 30% of income is manageable. Comparing options found a home that fits the month.

default.title: DIGITAL ARREST
default.speaker: 'Police officer'
default.text: Video call: a man in uniform says a parcel in your name had drugs. 'Pay ₹50,000 to clear your name or be arrested now!'

pocket_money.title: DIGITAL ARREST
pocket_money.speaker: 'Police officer'
pocket_money.text: A video call to Dad's phone: 'Your child's ID was used for a crime. Pay ₹50,000 now or we arrest them!'

scholarship.title: DIGITAL ARREST
scholarship.speaker: 'Police officer'
scholarship.text: A uniformed man on video: 'Your bank account was used for fraud. Pay ₹50,000 to verify or face arrest!'

earner.title: DIGITAL ARREST
earner.speaker: 'Police officer'
earner.text: Video call: 'A parcel in your name had drugs. Stay on camera, tell nobody, pay ₹50,000 now!'

choices.lesson: There is no such thing as 'digital arrest'. Real police never demand money on a video call.
choices.hint: Do real police arrest people over a video call?

choices.lesson: Staying on the call lets them build fear. Hang up. You don't have to prove anything to a caller.
choices.hint: Who benefits if you stay on the call?

choices.lesson: Hang up, then call 1930 or walk into a police station yourself. Real police never 'arrest' you on video.
Right move. Fear is their weapon, and talking to someone you trust breaks it.

default.title: SPREAD IT?
default.speaker: Aunty
default.intro: All four assets are made up. Returns vary and can be negative.
default.text: A ₹20,000 bonus to invest. Weather experts warn of a bad monsoon, but they're often wrong. Where does it go?

pocket_money.title: SPREAD IT?
pocket_money.speaker: Aunty
pocket_money.intro: All four assets are made up. Returns vary and can be negative.
pocket_money.text: Your first ₹20,000 bonus. A friend swears Mango Orchard 'always wins'. The radio warns of a weak monsoon.

scholarship.title: SPREAD IT?
scholarship.speaker: Aunty
scholarship.intro: All four assets are made up. Returns vary and can be negative.
scholarship.text: A ₹20,000 bonus. Last year Mango Orchard grew fastest; this year forecasts say weak rains. Where does it go?

earner.title: SPREAD IT?
earner.speaker: Aunty
earner.intro: All four assets are made up. Returns vary and can be negative.
earner.text: A ₹20,000 bonus. At the shop everyone talks about Mango Orchard. The monsoon looks shaky. Where does it go?

choices.lesson: One bet, one bad year, and 40% was gone. Big swings both ways: that's the risk you took.
choices.hint: What happens to a mango orchard in a bad monsoon?

effects.label: Mango fell, the other three held up

choices.lesson: Mango fell, but Banyan and Chai held up. Owning things that don't fail together is diversification.
No loss this year, but cash shrinks to inflation every year. Spreading wisely beats hiding.

default.title: HEALTH COVER
default.speaker: Insurance agent
default.text: Family health cover: about ₹1,500 a month. 'One hospital stay can cost ₹2 lakh.' Your buffer is ₹60,000.

pocket_money.title: HEALTH COVER
pocket_money.speaker: Clinic receptionist
pocket_money.text: Your parents are getting older. A family health cover costs about ₹1,500 a month. Your buffer: ₹60,000.

scholarship.title: HEALTH COVER
scholarship.speaker: Insurance agent
scholarship.text: A cousin's surgery cost ₹2 lakh last year. Health cover: about ₹1,500 a month. Your buffer: ₹60,000.

earner.title: HEALTH COVER
earner.speaker: Insurance agent
earner.text: Dad's knee needs surgery someday. Family cover: about ₹1,500 a month. Your buffer: ₹60,000.

choices.lesson: Insurance turns a huge, rare cost into a small, regular one. Comparing found the same cover for less.
Covered, good. Comparing two or three plans first usually finds the same cover cheaper.
A buffer covers a broken phone, not a hospital stay. Some risks are too big to carry alone.

default.title: CHIT FUND
default.speaker: Neighbour
default.text: 'My chit: ₹5,000 a month, 20 members. Not registered, but I promise 30% extra!' Everyone's joining.

pocket_money.title: CHIT FUND
pocket_money.speaker: Mom's friend
pocket_money.text: Mom's friend runs a chit: '₹5,000 a month, 30% extra, guaranteed. Registration is just paperwork.'

scholarship.title: CHIT FUND
scholarship.speaker: Neighbour
scholarship.text: 'Join my chit! ₹5,000 a month, 30% extra. No registration needed, we're all family here.'

earner.title: CHIT FUND
earner.speaker: Shop owner
earner.text: Your old boss runs a chit for shopkeepers: '₹5,000 a month, 30% extra. Not registered, but trust me.'

effects.label: The organiser vanished with the pot

choices.lesson: Unregistered + promised high returns + 'everyone's joining' is a classic trap. When it collapses, nobody can help.
choices.hint: Who checks on an unregistered organiser?

effects.label: Not registered, so you said no

choices.lesson: Registered chit funds have written rules and someone who checks on them. No registration means no protection.
Safe and steady. Boring beats vanishing.

default.title: CHILD'S FUTURE
default.speaker: Your child
default.text: Your 3-year-old: 'I'll be a doctor!' College is about 15 years away. Start a fund now, or later?

pocket_money.title: CHILD'S FUTURE
pocket_money.speaker: Your child
pocket_money.text: Your child wants to be a doctor. You remember how your parents scrambled for fees. College is 15 years away.

scholarship.title: CHILD'S FUTURE
scholarship.speaker: Your child
scholarship.text: Your child wants to be a doctor. A scholarship might help, or might not. College is 15 years away.

earner.title: CHILD'S FUTURE
earner.speaker: Your child
earner.text: You worked through college. Your child won't have to, if you plan. College is 15 years away.

choices.lesson: A named goal with a date, started early: 15 years of growth does the heavy lifting.
Starting 12 years late means saving many times more each month for the same goal. Goals need time.
choices.hint: How much a month if you only have 3 years?

choices.lesson: Gold's price moves up and down, and jewellery has making charges. Not wrong, but a named, growing fund is clearer.
